subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should owner-confirmed responsibility state become a core memory/plugin contract, remain a plugin or ClawHub-layer capability for now, or be split into narrower provenance and approval issues first?
rationale: The issue asks for a durable security and session-state trust model whose boundaries affect public plugin APIs, stored memory semantics, approvals, and future-context reuse, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Design Work
options.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers define narrower memory provenance, reuse-state, approval, and plugin-hook contracts before implementation.

options.title: Promote To Core Contract
options.body: Commit to owner-confirmed responsibility state as a core memory/plugin API and require compatibility, migration, and security review before code lands.

options.title: Prototype Outside Core
options.body: Route the behavior to a plugin or ClawHub prototype using existing hooks until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Split Into Narrow Design Work
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers define narrower memory provenance, reuse-state, approval, and plugin-hook contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current-main history touches plugin hook contracts, memory-state, and memory-host surfaces that would carry the design decision.
